questions.q: Which climate category does the Court give the island of Madeira?
questions.exp: The Court files Madeira as hot subtropical, Sherry as hot maritime and Port as warm to hot Mediterranean. Madeira is a mountainous Atlantic island off North Africa, its vines on steep terraced hillsides of volcanic soil in humid warmth.

questions.q: On the label of a Single Quinta Port, what does the Portuguese word quinta mean?
questions.exp: A quinta is a farm or wine estate in the Douro, so a Single Quinta Vintage Port comes from one property, often bottled in a good year the house does not declare. Harvest is colheita, the word for a single harvest tawny, while Late Bottled Vintage and most Vintage Port blend wine from several quintas.

questions.q: Which Sherry style is aged wholly by oxidation, with no flor at any stage?
questions.exp: Oloroso is fortified to about 17 per cent, too strong for flor to grow, so it ages in contact with air from the start and turns dark, nutty and dry. Fino and Manzanilla age under flor throughout and Amontillado begins under flor; the Court files Oloroso and Cream Sherry as its oxidative styles.

questions.q: Of these fortified wines, which keeps longest once opened?
questions.exp: Madeira has been heated and oxidised on purpose, so an opened bottle keeps for months with little change. Fino and Manzanilla fade within days like a white wine, and an opened Vintage Port is best drunk within a few days; the Court asks the shelf life of each once opened.

questions.q: In a Sherry solera, what is each tier of younger casks above the oldest row called?
questions.exp: A solera stacks butts by age: wine for bottling is drawn from the oldest row, the solera, and each loss is refilled from the next youngest tier, the criaderas or scales, so the young wine is schooled by the old. Running the scales is that drawing down and refilling, and criadera means nursery.

questions.q: Flor, the film that shields a Fino in cask, is made up of strains of which species?
questions.exp: Flor is a film of Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains that grows on wine of about 15 per cent alcohol in part filled butts, feeding on alcohol and glycerol and keeping air away. It gives Fino and Manzanilla their pale colour and bready, saline tang; Botrytis cinerea is noble rot, Aspergillus oryzae the koji mould of sake and Brettanomyces a spoilage yeast.

questions.q: Besides albariza and barros, what is the sandy soil of the Sherry zone called?
questions.exp: The Court names three Sherry soils: albariza, the white chalky soil that holds winter rain and gives the finest Palomino; barros, a darker clay; and arenas, sand near the coast long planted with Moscatel. Albariza ranks highest, while barros and arenas give heavier, coarser wine.

questions.q: What is the main city of the island of Madeira?
questions.exp: Funchal, on the island's sunny south coast, is Madeira's capital and main city, where the shippers' lodges have long aged the wine in their warm upper floors. The island lies in the Atlantic off North Africa, with volcanic soils and steep terraced hillsides.

questions.q: Which sweetness term on a Marsala label marks the sweetest style?
questions.exp: Marsala's sweetness terms are Secco, Semi-Secco and Dolce, the last carrying more than 100 grams of sugar per litre, and they stand beside its colours (Oro, Ambra, Rubino) and its ages (Fine, Superiore, Vergine). Abboccato is a general Italian word for a lightly sweet wine, not one of Marsala's terms.

questions.q: Which South African region does the Court name for fortified Muscat made from Muscat de Frontignan?
questions.exp: The Klein Karoo is a dry inland region of the Western Cape, behind the coastal mountains, known for fortified Muscadel from Muscat de Frontignan, the Muscat à Petits Grains. The Court pairs it with Rutherglen in Victoria as the fortified Muscats beyond Europe.

questions.q: Which fortified wine best suits a pecan pie, with its sugar, caramel and toasted nuts?
questions.exp: An aged Tawny Port has spent years in cask, so its sweetness carries walnut, caramel and dried fig that echo the pie and stand up to its sugar. Fino, Manzanilla and Sercial are dry, better with salted almonds, olives and seafood; the Court asks how sweetness, age and oxidation steer a fortified pairing.
